programs.nl_rule:
The input grid has a black background with a single 3x3 block of non-black colored cells. The block consists of nine distinct cells arranged in three rows: a top row, a middle row, and a bottom row, each containing three colored cells.

1. Locate the 3x3 block of non-black cells. Label its cells as: top-left (TL), top-center (TC), top-right (TR), mid-left (ML), center (C), mid-right (MR), bottom-left (BL), bottom-center (BC), bottom-right (BR).
2. The middle row becomes a horizontal axis spanning the full width of the grid. Fill every cell to the left of ML in that row with ML's color. Fill every cell to the right of MR in that row with MR's color. The center cell C remains unchanged.
3. From TC, draw a vertical ray upward (same column) using TC's color, extending to the top edge of the grid.
4. From TL, draw a diagonal ray going up-and-left (one step up, one step left per cell) using TL's color, until hitting a grid edge.
5. From TR, draw a diagonal ray going up-and-right (one step up, one step right per cell) using TR's color, until hitting a grid edge.
6. From BC, draw a vertical ray downward (same column) using BC's color, extending to the bottom edge of the grid.
7. From BL, draw a diagonal ray going down-and-left (one step down, one step left per cell) using BL's color, until hitting a grid edge.
8. From BR, draw a diagonal ray going down-and-right (one step down, one step right per cell) using BR's color, until hitting a grid edge.
9. The original 3x3 block cells remain in place. All other cells stay black.

The output grid has the same dimensions as the input grid. The background is black (.). The 3x3 block remains at its original position, with six rays emanating from the top and bottom rows and the middle row extended horizontally across the full grid width.

output_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.

tools.name: propose_inputs
tools.description: Submit candidate input grids you might show, several at once. The environment keeps the ones the verifier accepts, notes which leave the grid unchanged under the rule, and ranks the rest as candidates. Free: nothing is shown until you call show_transformed_input.

result.next: The environment asked a student 6 of your inputs; 6 came back wrong. It showed 1 of those as demonstration(s), worst first; 2 other wrong answer(s) flipped to correct after them.

content.text:
The environment indicates it already asked a student and showed demonstrations. Wait, but student_calls_left: 0. Hmm. It seems the environment automatically quizzes the student. Some wrong. Let me show more demonstrations maybe.

Actually the note says "student_calls_left": 0 — meaning query calls left is 0? Hmm. Let me not worry. Maybe I should show_transformed_input to teach more. But the automated process already showed 1 demonstration.

Hmm, actually the tool behaves as a batch: propose_inputs submits candidates and the environment queries a student. But student_calls_left 0 suggests no more query_student. But show_transformed_input may still work.

Let me show a couple more demonstrations to reinforce, particularly cases near edges. Actually the student is still wrong on 3 after shown 1. Wait "n_still_wrong": 3 out of 6 asked. Among n_asked 6, 6 wrong, 1 shown as demo, 2 flipped correct. So 3 still wrong.

I should show more demonstrations covering those. But I don't know which. I could show all my candidate inputs via show_transformed_input to ensure coverage. That adds demos. Let me show the ones likely problematic: edge cases (E top, F bottom, G left).

Actually show_transformed_input shows the pair, teaching. Let me show a few. But careful: the ones student already answers correctly would be redundant (but harmless for teaching, just logged).

Let me show the 8 inputs? That's a lot of calls. Let me show maybe the edge cases and a couple general ones.

Actually the goal: maximize exam score. More demonstrations help. Let me show all candidates as transformed inputs to ensure broad coverage. But only ones that are informative. Hmm.

The environment says it already showed 1. Let me show the 3 edge cases E, F, G. Actually let me show all which weren't shown. But we don't know which was shown.

Let me just do show_transformed_input for a few diverse ones: A (middle, square), E (top edge), F (bottom edge), G (left edge), H (non-square wide).

Then start_exam.

Let me call them in parallel.
